classification.difficultyReason: Identify the 18 deposits from birth through the 17th birthday, model their extra compounding period, and include the separate cash gift.

content.prompt: Each year on her birthday, Jane’s parents put $\$20$ into an investment account earning $9\frac{1}{2}\%$ per annum compound interest. The first deposit took place on the day of her birth. On her 18th birthday, Jane’s parents gave her the account and $\$20$ cash in hand.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How much money had Jane’s parents deposited in the account?

answer.worked:
The account receives deposits from birth to the 17th birthday, so there are 18 deposits.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total deposited}&=18(20)\\\text{Total deposited}&=\$360\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: How much money did she receive from her parents on her 18th birthday? Give your answer to the nearest cent.

answer.worked:
On the 18th birthday, the account contains
$$20(1.095)^{18}+20(1.095)^{17}+\cdots+20(1.095).$$
This is a geometric series with first term $a=20(1.095)$, common ratio $r=1.095$ and $n=18$.
$$\begin{align*}FV&=\frac{20(1.095)(1.095^{18}-1)}{1.095-1}\\FV&\approx\$950.27\end{align*}$$
Add the separate cash gift, retaining the unrounded account value until the final calculation:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total received}&=\frac{20(1.095)(1.095^{18}-1)}{1.095-1}+20\\\text{Total received}&\approx\$970.27\end{align*}$$
